instrument.state: An item or record passes through multiple handlers or locations, creating opportunities for substitution, alteration, contamination, or uncertainty about identity.
instrument.operation: Record each transfer and handling event with the responsible party, time, and purpose, then inspect that history for continuity and unexplained transitions.
instrument.signal: A continuous, internally consistent handling record links the examined item through its lifecycle, while gaps or contradictions identify breaks in documented custody.
instrument.inference: Documentary continuity supports the claim that the item examined is the item collected and that its handling history is accounted for; gaps weaken that provenance claim.
instrument.limit: Complete documentation does not itself prove that handlers recorded events truthfully or that no unrecorded alteration occurred, and missing records do not prove that alteration occurred. The strength of the inference depends on the reliability of the recording and safeguarding process.

target.question: What sequence of revision and assembly best explains the surviving novel draft, and which claims remain uncertain?

mapping.state:
The inquiry uses two provenance panels: A tracks an opening-section packet; B tracks a closing-section packet. The focal and comparison drafts use the same archive handling-ledger template. Each panel tracks identified leaves of its assigned draft; a matching ledger form does not stipulate that two drafts contain the same events.
Panel A is assigned to the novel draft under investigation.
Panel B is assigned to the novel draft under investigation.
mapping.operation:
Assign stable identifiers to leaves, record each witnessed handling or assembly event with responsible party, time and purpose, and audit the chain for unexplained transitions. Separate witnessed assembly from inferred composition and retain the event-specific evidence tags. Audit the two panels independently.
Constrain the focal draft reconstruction by the opening-section assembly-before-binding sequence only if the panel-A sequence inference applies to that draft.
Constrain the focal draft reconstruction by the closing-section replacement-after-review sequence only if the panel-B sequence inference applies to that draft.
mapping.signal: Panel A has a continuous reliable ledger and witnessed attachments placing its identified opening-section assembly before its dated binding event. Panel B has a continuous reliable ledger and witnessed attachments placing its identified closing-section replacement after its dated editorial review. Neither chain contains an unexplained transition in the interval examined.
mapping.inference:
For the novel draft under investigation, panel A supports the bounded sequence that its identified opening-section assembly preceded its recorded binding event.
For the novel draft under investigation, panel B supports the bounded sequence that its identified closing-section replacement followed its recorded editorial review.
Use of the same archive handling-ledger template establishes that the two drafts received the same internal shelf-label color.
Use of the same archive handling-ledger template establishes that the two drafts received the same internal box-label font.
Use of the same archive handling-ledger template establishes that the two drafts were entered using the same inventory-workstation model.
Use of the same archive handling-ledger template establishes that the two drafts received the same internal transport-slip border.
mapping.limit: Recording and safeguarding are reliable for the witnessed events stated here; no inference to unrecorded events, unchanged authorial intention or complete composition history is supplied. Ledger-template identity is the only stated cross-draft connection; shared authorship, leaf identity and assembly dates are not stipulated.
